topics.description: Gustavus Adolphus was king of Sweden who led Protestant forces during the Thirty Years' War and was killed at the Battle of Lützen in 1632.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One king of this country won the 1631 Battle of Breitenfeld (BRITE-en-feld) before dying at the Battle of Lutzen. Another king of this country, Charles XII, lost the Battle of Poltava and the Great Northern War to Peter the Great of Russia. One ruler of this country joined with (*) Denmark and Norway in the Kalmar Union. For ten points, the House of Vasa and its monarch Gustavus Adolphus ruled what Scandinavian country with capital at Stockholm?
parts.answer: Sweden [or Kingdom of Sweden or Sverige or Konungariket Sverige]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A king of this country established an aggressive light cavalry unit whose name translates to “cut them down.” A ruler of this country moved to Pope Alexander VII's court after converting to Catholicism and abdicating. That ruler had earlier invited (*) René Descartes to this country's court. Axel Oxenstierna served as regent of this country after its king died while leading a cavalry charge at the Battle of Lützen. In the early 17th century, this country was ruled by the Vasa dynasty, including the “Lion of the North” and his daughter, Christina. For 10 points, Gustavus Adolphus led what country with capital at Stockholm?
parts.answer: ANSWER: Sweden [or Kingdom of Sweden or Sverige or Konungariket Sverige]

topics.description: The U.S.-led military invasion of Iraq in 2003 that overthrew Saddam Hussein’s government and began the Iraq War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This politician called the laissez-faire policies of John Major “Anglo-Saxon ultraliberalism.” For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this two-time prime minister who became president of France from 1995 to 2007. For his  second term, he founded the new UMP party.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Chirac survived an assassination attempt in 2002 during this holiday, which commemorates the  storming of a Parisian prison that began the French Revolution on July 14, 1789.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Chirac commissioned a Bible scholar to write a briefing on Gog and Magog after being puzzled by  a metaphor in a 2003 phone call from the U.S. President arguing for this goal.
parts.answer: getting France to join in the U.S.-led coalition for the Iraq War [or answers referring to the  2003 Iraq War; or invasion of Iraq; or overthrow of Saddam Hussein]

topics.description: The U.S.-led war in Iraq from 2003 to 2011, beginning with the invasion that overthrew Saddam Hussein’s government.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Nuri al-Maliki tried to catch a shoe after it was thrown in protest of this war. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this war protested by Muntadhar al-Zaidi, during which Saddam Hussein was executed in its namesake country.
parts.answer: Iraq War [or Second Persian Gulf War; do not accept or prompt on “Persian Gulf War” alone]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Al-Zaidi threw his shoes at this president. This man served from 2001-2009 and was succeeded by Barack Obama.
parts.answer: George W. Bush [accept anything specifying the younger Bush; accept Bush 43; prompt on George Bush]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Bush appointed this first African-American Secretary of State, who gave a speech to the UN falsely claiming that Iraq had weapons of mass destruction.

topics.description: Rama is the regnal name used by kings of Thailand’s Chakri dynasty, including Ananda Mahidol as Rama VIII and Vajiralongkorn as Rama X.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about Marshal Phibun, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] After a 1932 coup in which Phibun came to power in this country governed from Bangkok, he changed its official name from Siam to a name meaning “land of the free.”
parts.answer: Thailand [or Kingdom of Thailand; or Ratcha-anachak Thai]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] After a failed monarchist revolt, Phibun installed to the throne a boy studying in Switzerland, Ananda Mahidol, who then gained this regnal name. The current king of Thailand also has this regnal name.
parts.answer: Rama [accept Rama VIII; accept Rama X]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During World War II, Phibun negotiated an alliance with this country, allowing its troops to pass through Thailand during the Burma Campaign.
parts.answer: Japan [or Nihon-koku; or Nippon-koku; or Empire of Japan; or Dai Nippon Teikoku; or Japanese Empire]

topics.description: The Islamic caliphate established by the Umayyad dynasty that ruled from Damascus from 661 to 750, with a later Umayyad branch continuing in al-Andalus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This was the official religion in the kingdoms of Alodia and Makuria. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this religion that was brought to both kingdoms by missionaries like Longinus. A nearby kingdom in the Horn of Africa that also practiced this religion was converted by Frumentius during the reign of its king Ezana.
parts.answer: Christianity [accept Coptic Orthodox Christianity; accept Greek Orthodox Christianity; accept Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Alodia and Makuria were both kingdoms along this river. The Coptic Church was based in Egypt, primarily in cities along this river.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Makurian king Kyriakos later invaded Egypt to free a Christian patriarch imprisoned by this caliphate. This caliphate was founded by Muawiyah I and ruled from Damascus until its fall in the Abbasid Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Rashidun caliphate spread Islam throughout much of the Middle East. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The caliphate was mostly composed of tribes of this ethnic group. Egypt, Iraq, and Algeria have large populations of this ethnic group, for which the peninsula containing Oman and Yemen is also named.
parts.answer: Arabs [generously accept word forms like Arabic or Arabian]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The caliphate conquered Syria and the Levant region from this empire, ruled by Heraclius at the time. This empire was also known as the Eastern Roman Empire and was led from Constantinople.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Following a civil war, the Rashidun Caliphate was replaced by a caliphate led by this dynasty, which eventually established itself in Spain even after its overthrow by the Abbasids.
parts.answer: the Umayyads [or al-ʾUmawīyūn, or Banū ʾUmayyah]

topics.description: The Japanese imperial state, especially the historical polity that expanded across East Asia and annexed Korea in 1910.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A citizen of one of these two polities, An Jung-Geun, assassinated the other’s first prime minister, Itō Hirobumi.  For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these two polities, one of which occupied a peninsula, and the other of which occupied a nearby  archipelago. Soldiers from one of these polities revolted against Emperor Gojong’s concessions to the other in the  Imo Mutiny.
parts.answer: Korean Empire and Empire of Japan [accept answers in either order; accept Joseon Dynasty in place of  Korea]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Japan influenced Gojong to enact the Gabo Reforms, the most notorious of which involved cutting this body  part, worn in the sangtu style by Korean males. The Qing Dynasty forced males to wear this body part in the queue style.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Japanese army horribly mistreated Koreans during this war, in which Japan decided bombing Pearl Harbor  was a great idea.
parts.answer: World War II [prompt on partial answer]

topics.description: Suleiman I was the longest-reigning Ottoman sultan, ruling during the empire’s sixteenth-century political, military, and cultural zenith.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire’s ruler Selim the Grim was the father of a man who would go on to expel the Knights Hospitaller from Rhodes. This empire was called the “Sick Man of Europe” before World War I, and it repurposed the Hagia Sophia as a mosque when it conquered (*) Constantinople in 1453. For ten points, what empire was ruled by Suleiman the Magnificent and would eventually be mostly replaced by Turkey?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This empire was modernized by the 19th century Tanzimat reforms. Young Christian boys were forced into this empire's elite Janissary corps. This empire, referred to as the “sick man of Europe,” reached its peak under (*) sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. The end of World War I brought on the dissolution of, for 10 points, what Islamic empire centered on modern day Turkey?

topics.description: The British practice of transporting convicted prisoners to Australian colonies, beginning with the First Fleet in 1788 and including penal settlements in Tasmania.

parts.label: L
parts.question: British colonists under George Arthur and indigenous inhabitants of this island fought in the 1820s  Black War. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this island, which was first settled by people crossing the Bass Strait. Europeans originally  called it Van Diemen's Land.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Martin Bryant killed 35 people in a Tasmanian city with this name. The Russo-Japanese War began  with a surprise attack at a Manchurian district with this name.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] About four out of every ten of these people who were sent to Australia came to Tasmania.  “Colonies” of these people were opened in Port Arthur as a means of correcting behavior.
parts.answer: convicts [or prisoners; or criminals; or transported people]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologized to the “stolen generations” of its indigenous people. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country that was discovered by Europeans after James Cook’s expedition landed at Botany Bay in present-day Sydney.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This was the name given to the indigenous people of Australia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Aborigines often conflicted with these specific people, who were first brought to Australia by the First Fleet. After becoming one of these people, Alfred Dreyfus was sent to live on Devil's Island.
parts.answer: convicts [or prisoners or convicted criminal; prompt on criminal alone]

topics.description: The Catholic ecumenical council held from 1545 to 1563 that clarified Catholic doctrine and initiated major reforms during the Counter-Reformation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man refused to recant his writings at the Diet of Worms. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this German theologian, who, angered by the Catholic Church’s use of indulgences, launched the Protestant Reformation by publishing his Ninety-FIve Theses.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Luther objected to the saying about indulgences beginning “as soon as [one of these items] in the coffer rings.” In the Middle Ages, the cheapest of these circular items of currency were often made from copper.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Church responded to the Protestant Reformation by holding this ecumenical council. This council condemned Protestant teachings and launched the Counter-Reformation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Martin Luther attacked this friar’s belief that remorse was not necessary for atonement if one bought an indulgence. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Dominican friar who sold indulgences with the slogan, “When the coin in the coffer rings / the soul from purgatory springs.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tetzel claimed that buying an indulgence would offer the buyer remission for these things, reducing the time spent in Purgatory. The Catholic Church recognizes seven “deadly” examples of these things, such as lust and wrath.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The sale of indulgences was eventually banned at this mid-16th century council, although the doctrine of Purgatory was affirmed. This council, convoked by Paul III, is often cited as the start of the Counter-Reformation.

topics.description: A Serbian secret military society involved in planning and supporting the 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In order to marry the lady-in-waiting Sophie Chotek, this man had to renounce his descendants’ rights to the throne. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this nephew of Emperor Franz Joseph I, who was assassinated in Sarajevo in 1914. This man’s death prompted the July Crisis, which eventually caused the escalations that led to World War I.
parts.answer: Franz Ferdinand [accept Archduke Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ferdinand was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip (PRIN-tzip), a member of the revolutionary movement Young Bosnia and one of a group of assassins working with this Serbian secret military society.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] As the eldest son of Archduke Karl Ludwig of this country, Ferdinand was the heir presumptive to its throne. The union of this country and Hungary was allied with the German Empire in World War I.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Oskar Potiorek encouraged rioting after this event, whose participants were sentenced to death in the  Salonika Trial. One participant in this event failed to kill himself after ingesting expired cyanide and jumping  into a river 13 centimeters deep. The July Ultimatum was issued after this event, which was planned by the  (*) Black Hand and carried out by Gavrilo Princip. For 10 points, name this murder of an Austro-Hungarian  archduke, which led to the outbreak of World War I.
parts.answer: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand [prompt on partial answer; accept reasonable equivalents,  such as the killing of Franz Ferdinand]
